name: Conn (Con)

attributes.attribute: bears the name of the god Lugh
reshaped Celtic names for the lay reader

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The record here turns to the fairy faith of the Celts and to the naming of Celtic figures. The fairy belief shows religious features. Legend says the fairies were once gods. The leprechaun, for one, carries the name of the god Lugh. Some scholars reject the link between folk figures and the old gods. Others find resonances between the two. The hero Ass of the tales appears in folklore as the giant Finn McCool. Celtic religion did not start in writing. It started in oral story. Transcribers spelled names in many ways, and later authors anglicised them for the English reader.

okr.objective: The record treats fairy belief and the varying spellings of Celtic names.
key_results: The fairy faith shows religious features.
